name: Minnesota

context: MN 340: Cover crops reduce erosion from wind and water; time them to protect soil in the critical erosion periods.
MN 589: Cross wind trap strips are herbaceous strips perpendicular to the most erosive winds on cropland with a wind erosion concern.
cover_rules: MN 340: Single species cereal rye must be planted by November 1st across Minnesota; do not seed into frozen ground.
MN 340: Planting depth should be between 0.75 and 1.5 inches. For the no-till seeding rate the STIR value must be below 20.
MN 340: Plant the cover crop as early as possible and terminate as late as practical; leave residues on the surface after termination.
residue: MN 329: Keep a minimum of 60 percent residue cover (flat) on the soil surface when no living canopy covers the soil.
MN 345: For wind erosion, set the height of standing residue after harvest and the row direction; crop interval STIR no greater than 80.
MN 329: Leave crop stubble at 80% of the plant stalk height to hold snow and moisture.
barriers: MN 589: Cross wind trap strips are at least 15 feet wide if vegetation is 1 foot or more tall, and at least 25 feet if under 1 foot.
MN 585: Stripcropping strips run perpendicular to prevailing wind, with at least 50 percent of the rotation in erosion-resistant crops.
MN 588: Cross wind ridges stay within 45 degrees of perpendicular to erosive wind; spacing no more than four times ridge height.
windbreak: MN 380: Density 50-65% uses twin-row deciduous shrubs or 1-row conifers; 65+% (NTE 80%) uses 3 or more rows of conifers, deciduous trees and shrubs.
MN 380: Replace dead stock and control competing vegetation for at least 3 years to establish the windbreak.
roughening: MN 609: Tillage must give random roughness that cuts potential wind erosion by 25 percent; begin on the windward edge of the field.
MN 588: Cross wind ridges suit loamy and clayey soils and are not well adapted to sandy soils.
grazing: MN 528: Meet the minimum stubble height for the vegetation type set in the Grazing Management Plan to prevent wind erosion.
drought: MN 528: Longer rest periods will be needed between grazing events during drought conditions to ensure adequate plant recovery.
MN 528: Rest periods during drought conditions may be 90 days or more.
seeding: MN 327: Dormant season seeding (fall or frost seeding) is recommended for pollinator native plantings, using a no-till native drill.
pasture: MN 512: Select plants giving maximum ground cover to protect soil from wind and water erosion; a perennial with a nurse crop speeds ground cover.
disturbed: MN 342: Critical area planting stabilizes areas with high wind or water erosion, such as mined lands and construction sites.
dunes: MN 342: Critical area planting is used to stabilize areas such as sand dunes.

cover.name: Cereal rye
cover.rate: 40 lbs/acre PLS minimum if planted July 15th-October 1st; 100 PLS lbs/acre in the PM Tech Note 6 table

coverPlant.text: MN 340: Single species cereal rye July 15th-October 1st at 40 lbs/acre; after October 1st 50 to 75 lbs/acre. Plant by November 1st.

seedWin.text: MN 327: South of I-94, seed April 1 - June 1 or August 1 – September 10.
MN 327: North of I-94, seed April 1 - June 15 or July 15 - September 1.
